topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture series, introduces the speaker, and sets out the core learning outcomes regarding cancer etiology and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Origins of Cancer: Intrinsic Errors, Environment, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the fundamental origins of cancer by comparing intrinsic biological processes, inherited genetics, and environmental exposures through epidemiological data.

topics.label: Infectious Agents and Pathogen-Driven Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how viral, bacterial, and parasitic infections drive cancer development, with a focused examination of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Direct and Metabolically Activated Mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how physical radiation, dietary toxins, and chemical carcinogens undergo metabolic activation to induce DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic mechanisms of tumorigenesis, focusing on how tumor promoters, chronic inflammation, and developmental timing drive cancer development.

topics.label: Methods for Detecting and Assessing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to determine carcinogenicity and assess human exposure risk.
